newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Yeltsin to meet in March - White House.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Yeltsin to meet in March - White House.

text.p: The White House confirmed on Thursday President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin will meet in March, but did not set a date or venue.

The two leaders spoke by telephone for about 20 minutes on Thursday morning and agreed to meet in March, the White House said in a statement. It said that a scheduled February meeting between U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomydrin would prepare for the summit.
White House officials said it was the United States' turn to host such a meeting because Clinton and Yeltsin last met in Moscow in April.

But they added that because of Yeltsin's health, it was possible that the two leaders might meet in a third country closer to Russia or even in Moscow. Yeltsin underwent quintuple bypass surgery last month and is still recovering.

Earlier, Russia's Interfax news agency quoted Kremlin press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying the two men would meet in March, and a Russian presidential spokesman confirmed the report to Reuters.

The White House said Clinton told Yeltsin during Thursday's phone call -- their first conversation since Yeltsin's surgery -- that he was pleased at his continuing recovery, and the Russian leader congratulated Clinton on his re-election last month.
